info.title: FlashData Developer API
info.description: API-key authenticated data, jobs, bulk collections and account reads, plus public discovery. Source snapshot: 2026-10-19.

get.summary: Read the public component status summary
List public source capabilities without account-specific pricing
List public USD plans and prices
Read the calling API key's authorized sources and result origin
get.description:
Free, header-only X-API-Key authentication. Returns only granted public
source names and the configured signed-result storage origin (null if
unavailable). No account ID, key ID, secret or storage credentials are returned.
Local MCP revalidates this endpoint before every tool discovery and call,
including cached result reads. No query parameters or request body are accepted.
All /api-access routes share 120 requests per minute per client IP and return
Cache-Control private, no-store. Normal key last-used tracking still occurs.

200.description: Authorized public sources and result origin

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read the live account balance using an API key
get.description:
Free X-API-Key read of the authenticated account's Redis balance, shared by
all account keys. In-flight reservations can affect the balance. Does not
fabricate reservedCredits, fall back to Mongo, or turn failures into zero.
No query parameters or request body. Shares the /api-access read limit;
responses are private, no-store. Does not reserve or spend Credits.

200.description: Signed balance and nonnegative available Credits

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read actual account prices for sources authorized by the API key
get.description:
Free X-API-Key read of live subscription prices, restricted to granted
sources. Missing prices are unavailable with null values, never replaced
with Catalog defaults. request_count counts calls, not search results;
download estimates instead expose the per-TB rate (10^12 bytes).
Estimates do not reserve Credits or guarantee future admission.
Only the documented query parameters are accepted; no request body.
Shares the /api-access read limit; responses are private, no-store.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: A source granted to this key; omit to read all granted sources.

parameters.name: request_count
parameters.description: Decimal integer number of calls; does not estimate download size.

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read account plan limits and current pending jobs using an API key
get.description:
Free X-API-Key read of account-wide concurrency, batch and pending ceilings,
plus the current pending count. These separate snapshots do not represent
remaining concurrency slots or an atomic admission promise. No query
parameters or request body. Shares the /api-access read limit; responses
are private, no-store. Does not reserve or spend Credits.

200.description: Plan ceilings and current pending count

429.description: Too many account reads; retry after the rate-limit window

get.summary: Read account usage for sources authorized by the API key
get.description:
Free read, authenticated only by X-API-Key. Includes all account keys but
only sources granted to the calling key. Does not return query text, keys,
payment details or other accounts. Defaults to seven days; maximum 31 days.
Dates must use UTC Z timestamps. From is inclusive and to exclusive;
both are rounded down to minutes. With from alone, to defaults to from + 7 days.
With neither, to is the start of the next minute. Aggregates are eventually
consistent; even updating=false does not guarantee all recent events are ingested.
Read limit: 60 requests per minute per client IP.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: An exact catalog source granted to the calling key; omitted means all granted sources.

200.description: Scoped request counts and charged Credits, with freshness information

429.description: Too many usage reads; retry after the rate-limit window

post.summary: Create a bulk YouTube job and obtain a direct R2 upload URL
post.description: Creates an awaiting-upload coordinator record. Upload a UTF-8 text file containing one 11-character YouTube video ID per line to upload.href, then call the start operation. The file can be streamed and may contain millions of IDs.

201.description: Bulk job created with a 15-minute direct upload URL

get.summary: Read bulk job progress and aggregate counts

patch.summary: Change parameters for IDs that have not yet been admitted
patch.description: Partially merges options into the encrypted bulk configuration. This is allowed while awaiting upload or while paused before input scanning completes. Already-admitted child jobs keep the parameters with which they were created. A pause may briefly finish its current admission slice; retry a 409 update after the coordinator releases that slice. Set callback_url to null to clear it.

delete.summary: Stop admitting new items for a bulk job
delete.description: Already-admitted child jobs may finish and retain their normal charges.

post.summary: Start scanning an uploaded YouTube ID file
post.description: Accepts a non-empty UTF-8 video ID file up to 2 GiB (2147483648 bytes). Pins the uploaded object's size and ETag before any child job is admitted.

200.description: Bulk job started or its current idempotent state

post.summary: Pause bulk admission and coordinator finalization
post.description: Stops admitting new child jobs and suspends coordinator finalization. A child job already admitted to a worker queue is not interrupted and keeps its original parameters and charge.

200.description: Paused bulk job or its current idempotent state

post.summary: Resume a manually or automatically paused bulk job

get.description: Redirects to private R2. The manifest and its result parts remain available for 24 hours after the entire bulk job completes; management never proxies result bytes.

200.description: JSON manifest returned by R2 after the client follows the redirect

get.summary: Download one gzip-compressed NDJSON bulk result part

get.description: Authenticates access and redirects to a short-lived private R2 URL. The management service never proxies the result body. Clients that follow the redirect receive the JSON result directly from R2. Stored results expire 24 hours after completion.

options.description: Reused for every ID. Metadata accepts include_formats and include_chapters. Transcript and captions accept language and auto. Trainability accepts no source options. These four data sources optionally accept result_storage. Supported storage_type values are s3, s3_compatible, oss, gcs, azure, cos, bos, and tos. storage_url is the bucket name (Azure container name); object_prefix is optional. S3, S3-compatible, OSS, COS, BOS, and TOS use access_key and secret_key. S3-compatible and OSS also require a public HTTPS endpoint_url. COS, BOS, and TOS require region and use fixed provider endpoints. COS bucket names include the APPID. BOS S3-compatible HTTPS delivery supports bj, su, and hkg. GCS requires service_account with project_id, client_email, and private_key. Azure requires account_name and a container SAS sas_token with write permission. Default object_prefix is YYYYMMDD, frozen to the UTC bulk creation date. Files are written to <prefix>/<source>/<bulkId>/results/part-NNNNNNNN.jsonl.gz; manifest.json in the same bulk directory is written last. Each JSONL row includes its input index and completed, failed, or invalid status. Internal R2 results remain available through the result links for 24 hours. Download accepts the normal YouTube download parameters, requires customer storage, and does not permit browser_delivery. Download storage supports the same eight provider types and credential shapes listed above under the storage field. Download storage may include object_prefix; YYYYMMDD tokens resolve to the UTC upload date, while literal prefixes are unchanged.

includedCredits.description: Credits included in each paid subscription cycle; zero for Pay As You Go.

credits.description: Credits granted by a successful one-time top-up; zero for recurring prices.

googlePer1kCents.description: Google request price per 1,000 successful requests, in USD cents.

youtubePer1kCents.description: Standard YouTube request price per 1,000 successful requests, in USD cents.

downloadPerTbCents.description: Download price per decimal TB (1,000,000,000,000 bytes), in USD cents.

maxApiRequests.description: Maximum free API calls when the entire trial grant is spent on the lowest-cost per-request API at current Pay as you go rates. Other APIs may allow fewer calls. Downloads are billed by delivered bytes and excluded from this count.

googleSearchRequests.description: Requests if the entire grant is spent on Google sources, using the highest current source rate.

youtubeDataRequests.description: Standard YouTube requests, excluding Extended Search, using the highest current source rate.

downloadGigabytes.description: Approximate delivered media volume in decimal GB (1 GB = 1000000000 bytes). Zero when the grant cannot cover the initial download reservation. Completion also depends on per-job reservations and settlement.
